Patel expressed dismay that Modi remained in London for seven years. She believes India was angry over Britain's stance on his extradition. India has denied opposing the return of illegal migrants.

title: ‘Verifying authenticity’: DRDO sources on report claiming DRDO data put on dark web

A cyber intelligence firm discovered the sensitive information during routine monitoring. The Defence Research and Development Organisation is currently verifying the authenticity of these claims. Cybersecurity specialists urge immediate forensic verification of the alleged data breach.

title: US updates list of H-1B debarred & disqualified cos; names these as 'willful violators'

title: Abhishek meets Om Birla, seeks early decision on disqualification of 20 rebel MPs

title: Mehbooba faces heat over Jantar Mantar comment, oppn accuses her justifying use of force

Other parties also condemned her comments, highlighting past suffering in Kashmir.

title: Jeff Bezos ex-wife MacKenzie Scott helped write a 'donation playbook' for Snap founder

This significant contribution will benefit over 261,000 Californians facing financial hardship.  The donation follows a model pioneered by MacKenzie Scott, who has given billions to nonprofits.  The funds will be channeled through Undue Medical Debt, a prominent organization.  This initiative targets vulnerable residents, alleviating burdens of unpayable medical bills.

title: From pacifist to talks of going nuclear: China shaken as Japan breaks 80-yr-old shackles
content: Japan is shifting away from its long-standing pacifist security doctrine, with increasing defense budgets and a major enhancement of military skills. The nation has restarted arms exports and is forming a dedicated intelligence agency. China perceives these changes as a profound provocation and an emerging strategy, sparked by modern threats and regional shifts in the geopolitical landscape.

title: 6 orphaned rhinos rescued from poachers have all given birth in the wild

Their successful births signify a remarkable milestone in conservation efforts, providing renewed hope for endangered rhino populations. Wildlife officials emphasized that these births not only enrich the local ecosystem but also bolster South Africa's commitment to preserving this majestic species.

title: No H-1B visa, two layoffs, then a job at Silicon Valley tech giant

title: Murder, robbery, rape accused among 989 with criminal records at CJP's Jantar Mantar stir

title: Quote of the Day by Pythagoras: Why reflecting on your mistakes each night leads to a better life

title: Pickaxe Mountain revives the Kahuta question: Could India have hit Pakistan’s nuclear leap?
content: The West Asia conflict highlights Iran’s nuclear ambitions and US-Israeli efforts to block them. Pickaxe Mountain, housing hidden nuclear facilities, has become a focal point. Strikes on Natanz in 2025 echoed earlier pre-emptive attacks on nuclear programmes worldwide, from Allied raids on Germany’s heavy-water plant in WWII to Israel’s operations against Iraq’s Osiraq reactor (1981) and Syria’s al-Kibar site (2007). India, however, refrained from striking Pakistan’s Kahuta facility in the 1980s, a decision that enabled Pakistan’s nuclearisation. To avoid escalation, India and Pakistan signed a 1988 accord prohibiting attacks on nuclear sites. India now prioritises survivability through layered missile defence projects.
